owner_route: role:ea-product-owner; semantic review by role:ea-definitions-owner; principals unassigned

definitions.statement: An Engineering Role Profile is a versioned description of one engineering role and level, its actual tasks, critical incidents, required capabilities, working conditions and success criteria, selected before assessment design.
definitions.scope: One employer or declared role family and level.
boundaries: A job title alone is not a Role Profile.
A profile does not prove a case predicts success.
definitions.intuition: A concrete picture of the job to assess, including what engineers actually do and what good work looks like at that level.

definitions.statement: A Target Outcome is a predeclared, independently observed performance criterion for role R in population P at horizon T and hiring capacity C, with raters, components and missing-data rules fixed before assessment scores are analyzed.
definitions.scope: One named validation study and role context.
boundaries: The assessment score or hiring decision cannot serve as its own outcome.
One employer's outcome is not a universal best-engineer definition.

parameters.name: C
parameters.interpretation: Positive count of candidates selected under the policy; selection fraction is derived from the declared pool size.

definitions.intuition: The later work result we would use to judge whether the assessment helped, chosen before seeing assessment scores.

definitions.statement: An Assessment Construct is a named capability or behavior the assessment intends to infer, with observable indicators, rival explanations, role linkage and a declared interpretation limit.
definitions.scope: One exploratory challenge or role-linked assessment design, with the intended use declared.
boundaries: A construct name does not prove it can be measured.
Creativity, analysis and ingenuity remain distinct hypotheses until evidence supports their structure.
definitions.intuition: The capability we hope an answer reveals, together with what else could explain the same answer.

definitions.statement: A Case Family is a controlled set of prompts sharing an intended reasoning operation and scoring blueprint while varying surface content, constraints and exposure history.
definitions.scope: Question generation, comparison and item-bank governance.
boundaries: Family membership does not establish equal difficulty.
A familiar riddle and an unreleased variant may have different exposure effects.
definitions.intuition: A group of questions built around the same reasoning task, even when their stories and objects differ.

definitions.statement: A Case Version is an immutable administered prompt sequence with source, family, allowed information reveals, timing, media, accessibility alternatives, scoring blueprint and exposure state pinned by content identity.
definitions.scope: One frozen administration form.
boundaries: Editing a prompt creates a new version.
Novel wording does not establish quality or equivalence.
definitions.intuition: The exact question form a person saw, including clues, timing and accessibility rules.

definitions.statement: An Assessment Session is one participant's bounded encounter with one Case Version under a pinned administration policy, producing at most ten minutes of recorded answer and an attributable event history.
definitions.scope: One of at most three sessions in an assessment attempt.
boundaries: The session is not the candidate or the score.
Preparation time and accommodations require explicit policy rather than silent inference.
definitions.intuition: One bounded encounter in which a participant answers one frozen case.

definitions.statement: A Candidate Response is the source recording and ordered answer events produced in an Assessment Session, with exact custody identity and participant correction history.
definitions.scope: One session response under one purpose and consent state.
boundaries: A response is an observation, not a trait or performance conclusion.
The recording does not grant research reuse or public release.
definitions.intuition: The participant’s original recorded answer and its event history, before a transcript or score interprets it.

definitions.statement: A Transcript is a versioned text rendering of a Candidate Response with method, uncertainty markers and corrections linked to the immutable source recording.
definitions.scope: Speech-to-text and participant-corrected representations.
boundaries: A transcript is not the response original.
Transcript confidence is not scoring confidence.
definitions.intuition: A text rendering of the recorded answer that can contain errors and corrections.

definitions.statement: A Rubric is a frozen set of construct-linked observable criteria, anchored performance levels, alternative-valid-answer rules and missing-evidence handling for specified Case Versions.
definitions.scope: One formative or role-linked assessment purpose and compatible case set.
boundaries: A rubric is not evidence of validity.
A canonical punchline cannot be the sole creativity criterion.
definitions.intuition: The anchored criteria used to judge observable parts of an answer, including valid unexpected approaches.

definitions.statement: A Scoring Run is a reproducible application of one pinned Rubric and scorer configuration to one pinned response/transcript input, producing criterion ratings, cited evidence, uncertainty and errors.
definitions.scope: Human, model-assisted or model-generated rating under a declared method.
boundaries: A scoring receipt does not prove the score is valid.
A model may suggest ratings but cannot grant employment-use authority.
definitions.intuition: One reproducible attempt to apply a pinned rubric and scorer to a pinned answer.

definitions.statement: A Score Report is a purpose-limited presentation of Scoring Run results, criterion evidence, uncertainty, missing observations, correction status and permitted interpretation.
definitions.scope: Participant feedback or separately governed employer use.
boundaries: A challenge report cannot silently become a hiring decision.
A percentile requires an identified comparison population and calibrated forms.
definitions.intuition: The purpose-limited view of ratings, evidence, gaps and uncertainty shown to an allowed reader.

definitions.statement: A Feedback Metric is one versioned participant-facing value or status in a Score Report, derived from pinned case, rubric, scoring and administration evidence by a declared calculation and display rule, with its unit, missingness, uncertainty, comparison scope and permitted interpretation recorded.
definitions.scope: One named metric version, report purpose, case or session scope and intended audience.
boundaries: A displayed value is not a validated ability or employment prediction merely because it is numeric.
Administrative coverage, transcript quality and completion must not be presented as candidate ability.
A metric cannot use an uncalibrated peer population as a percentile or role-fit reference.
definitions.intuition: It is one clearly explained number, label or status shown to a developer, together with the evidence and limits needed to read it correctly.

definitions.statement: A Product Success Metric is a versioned, decision-linked measure of whether a declared product value or risk condition is met in a specified population and phase, with its numerator, denominator or outcome scale, observation window, source, missing-data rule, uncertainty, comparison and owner-selected decision rule recorded before interpretation.
definitions.scope: One product capability, experiment or phase gate and declared participant, employer or study population.
boundaries: A pilot engagement or satisfaction measure cannot establish hiring validity.
A score's ability to predict future work is evaluated against independent outcomes, not report views or rater agreement.
A target or dashboard color does not authorize a product claim or deployment decision.
definitions.intuition: It says exactly what would count as product progress, for whom and over what period, while keeping usage, measurement quality and real-world value separate.

definitions.statement: A Validation Study is a preregistered, source-pinned comparison of assessment policies against independently specified outcomes, populations, costs and error analyses, with development and held-out evidence kept distinct.
definitions.scope: One claim, role and target-use context.
boundaries: Rater agreement alone is not predictive validity.
A voluntary challenge cohort alone cannot establish employer deployment validity.
definitions.intuition: A registered test of whether an assessment claim holds against independent evidence.

definitions.statement: A Claim Tier is a bounded statement of what the current evidence permits the product owner to say or use, ordered from idea through reproducibility, reliability, prediction, accepted selection and observed value.
definitions.scope: Public, participant and employer communications for one product version.
boundaries: Higher tier is not inherited from a lower tier.
Changing role, language, model or population can invalidate an earlier tier.
definitions.intuition: A named level of product claim whose evidence and use limits are explicit.

definitions.statement: A Consent Record is attributable evidence that a participant gave or withdrew consent for one named processing purpose when the approved protocol uses consent as that purpose's lawful basis, bound to exact notice wording, scope and time.
definitions.scope: One participant, consent-based purpose and notice version.
boundaries: A Purpose Choice may be recorded even when consent is not the selected lawful basis; it must not be relabeled as a Consent Record.
Challenge participation does not imply research, model-training or employment-use consent.
definitions.intuition: Evidence that a person made a specific informed choice for a specific approved purpose when consent is the selected basis.

definitions.statement: A Cohort is a defined set of participants selected by declared eligibility, recruitment, time window and sampling process for one research or validation purpose.
definitions.scope: One study and its analysis populations.
boundaries: Self-selected challengers are not automatically representative of applicants.
Cohort membership alone does not grant data access.
definitions.intuition: The declared group of people or responses to which a study or comparison applies.

definitions.statement: A Decision Policy is a frozen mapping from specified score inputs and uncertainty to a selection action at a stated capacity, with abstention, human review, accommodation and appeal rules.
definitions.scope: One role, population, employer, jurisdiction and claim tier.
boundaries: A model score does not enact a hiring decision.
A policy is not effective until the employer and applicable owners authorize that exact use.
definitions.intuition: The versioned rule that turns eligible evidence into an allowed recommendation or action under owner control.

definitions.statement: A Criterion Rating is one anchored judgment about one elicited rubric dimension of one response, made by an identified rater or pinned scorer with cited answer evidence and an explicit missingness state.
definitions.scope: One response, dimension, case version, rater, mode and score version.
boundaries: A rating is an observation under a rubric, not a direct measure of a stable trait.
Not elicited and unknown evidence must not be converted to zero.
definitions.intuition: The rating describes what this answer showed on this criterion under these exact conditions.

definitions.statement: An Independent Criterion is a separately elicited and scored observation of work-relevant performance used to test whether an assessment score transfers beyond its own case, with outcome assessors masked to that score.
definitions.scope: One validation study and declared performance domain.
boundaries: A similar question scored by the same rubric is not an independent criterion.
A laboratory work sample is not automatically later job performance or the study's Target Outcome.
definitions.intuition: It checks the answer against a different piece of work rather than against itself.

definitions.statement: A Response Mode is a versioned way a participant receives a case or expresses an answer, including spoken recording, corrected transcript, text or diagram, with its timing and accommodation conditions.
definitions.scope: One case administration and scoring comparison.
boundaries: Mode availability does not establish score equivalence.
A correction of ASR text is not a new source recording.
definitions.intuition: It records how the same intended task reached the person and how their answer was captured.

definitions.statement: A Rater is a human evaluator assigned to apply a pinned Rubric independently under documented training, masking and conflict rules; automated scorers are separate pinned configurations.
definitions.scope: One study and permitted rubric dimensions.
boundaries: Expert status does not make a rating ground truth.
Adjudication does not erase original independent ratings.
definitions.intuition: A rater is a person whose judgment can itself vary and must be measured.

definitions.statement: A Scoring Specification is a versioned rule set mapping elicited Criterion Ratings and declared missingness to session and optional composite scores, uncertainty and permitted interpretations for one declared formative or role-linked purpose.
definitions.scope: One score version and compatible role, cases, rubrics and modes.
boundaries: A formula alone does not validate what a score means.
Changing weights, transformations or missingness rules creates a new score version.
definitions.formal_expression: S_v = f_v(ratings, missingness, case, role, mode)
definitions.intuition: It is the recipe that turns evidence-based ratings into a reportable number and states when that number should not be used.

definitions.statement: Measurement Uncertainty is the estimated range or decision instability of a score arising from sampled cases, raters, response modes, transcription and model fit under a named measurement design.
definitions.scope: One score version, population and intended decision.
boundaries: Rater agreement alone is not total score uncertainty.
An interval estimated with multiple research cases cannot be applied to a one-case product without a design study.
definitions.formal_expression: P(decision changes | plausible case, rater, mode replacements, design)

notation.design: actual number and allocation of cases, raters and modes

definitions.intuition: It asks whether a reasonable repeat of the assessment would lead to the same conclusion.

definitions.statement: A Calibration Set is a versioned collection of responses and ratings assigned before validation to train raters, refine anchors, fit permitted scoring parameters and find failure cases.
definitions.scope: One development phase and pinned score version.
boundaries: Results on the Calibration Set are development evidence, not held-out validation.
A response used to tune a model cannot later become untouched test evidence for that model.
definitions.intuition: This is where the scoring procedure is learned and repaired.

definitions.statement: A Validation Holdout is a preassigned participant, case-family, employer or time slice whose outcome labels and responses do not influence case, rubric, scorer, weights or analysis choices before its locked evaluation.
definitions.scope: One preregistered validation comparison.
boundaries: Repeated inspection and retuning destroys holdout status.
A participant split alone does not test transfer to new case families or employers.
definitions.intuition: It is the untouched test of whether the frozen method works elsewhere.

definitions.statement: An Estimand is the exact population-level quantity a study intends to learn, specifying population, outcome, policies or conditions compared, capacity, time horizon and treatment of missing outcomes before estimating it.
definitions.scope: One registered hypothesis or decision comparison.
boundaries: An observed sample statistic is an estimate, not the estimand itself.
Top-capacity utility for all applicants is not identified from hired-only outcomes without additional design and assumptions.

notation.U: selection utility defined for the target population and outcome

definitions.intuition: It states precisely what difference the experiment is trying to estimate before the data arrive.

definitions.statement: Case Exposure is a versioned record of where and when a case or its underlying solution mechanism may have been seen, practiced, shared or leaked by a population, including uncertainty about that history.
definitions.scope: One case family or version and recruitment population.
boundaries: Unreleased wording does not prove an unrehearsed reasoning pattern.
Self-reported familiarity is incomplete evidence of exposure.
definitions.intuition: It tracks whether the task is still fresh enough to test reasoning rather than recall.

definitions.statement: A Decision Threshold is a predeclared boundary in a specified score and uncertainty scale that a Decision Policy may use for an action, justified for one role, population and capacity with an explicit review or abstention region.
definitions.scope: One authorized policy version.
boundaries: A display percentile or convenient cut point is not an authorized threshold.
A threshold does not transfer across changed cases, scorers, modes or populations without bridging evidence.
definitions.intuition: It is the point where an uncertainty-aware policy changes its recommendation, if that exact use has been validated and authorized.

definitions.statement: Analytical Reasoning is the case-bounded ability to represent supplied facts and constraints, distinguish assumptions from evidence, compare causal explanations and test whether a proposed conclusion follows.
definitions.scope: Session 1 tasks and role-linked independent work criteria.
boundaries: Knowing a riddle's familiar answer is not evidence of analytical reasoning by itself.
A session rating cannot establish a stable general reasoning trait without cross-case evidence.
definitions.intuition: It is how the candidate makes sense of the problem and checks their logic.

definitions.statement: Creative Reasoning is the case-bounded production and evaluation of a non-obvious approach that is useful under the stated goal and constraints, judged for quality rather than answer quantity or rarity alone.
definitions.scope: Session 1 tasks and independent creative engineering work.
boundaries: Original wording, many ideas or surprising but unusable proposals do not suffice.
The assessment cannot claim broad workplace creativity without transfer evidence.
definitions.intuition: It is finding a fresh answer that could actually work.

definitions.statement: Ingenuity is a case-bounded, feasible change in framing, mechanism or use of available resources that resolves a constraint while preserving the goal.
definitions.scope: Session 1 tasks with a fair opportunity to reframe or adapt.
boundaries: A trick answer without an explained mechanism is insufficient.
Ingenuity may overlap with creative and analytical reasoning; distinctness is a hypothesis to test.
definitions.intuition: It is the workable move that changes how the problem can be solved.

definitions.statement: Technical and Product Design Judgment is role-level reasoning that translates user goals and engineering constraints into a coherent software design, explains quality-attribute tradeoffs and operating risks, and revises the design when requirements change.
definitions.scope: Session 2 cases and independently rated engineering design work.
boundaries: A spoken design is not evidence of coding or implementation throughput.
Familiar architecture vocabulary without causal fit to requirements does not meet the construct.
definitions.intuition: It is choosing and explaining a design that fits the product need and survives a changed constraint.

definitions.statement: Cooperation Judgment is case-bounded reasoning about other parties' incentives, mutual commitments, allocation of work and credit, conflict repair and adaptation to a counterparty response.
definitions.scope: Session 3 hypothetical cases and comparison with observed coordination.
boundaries: Stating the socially approved answer does not establish cooperative behavior.
Cooperation does not require yielding when that would breach a safety, fairness or user constraint.
definitions.intuition: It is planning a workable joint action while accounting for what others need and may do.

definitions.statement: Communication Judgment is the case-bounded quality of a proposed message or explanation in making relevant facts, requests, commitments, uncertainty and next steps understandable to the intended collaborators.
definitions.scope: Session 3 work cases and observed team coordination criteria.
boundaries: Accent, speaking speed, confidence and social style are not substitutes for message content.
A polished hypothetical message is not proof of later workplace communication behavior.
definitions.intuition: It is whether the other person could understand and act on the message.

definitions.statement: A High-Performing Engineer is a person whose independently observed, opportunity-aware performance meets a predeclared Target Outcome standard for one Engineering Role Profile, population and time horizon.
definitions.scope: One validation claim with fixed role, outcome and threshold.
boundaries: There is no universal best-engineer label in this model.
An assessment rank or hiring decision cannot define its own successful outcome.
definitions.intuition: The phrase only has meaning after the role and the evidence of good work are specified.

definitions.statement: A Case Generator is a pinned human- or machine-assisted procedure that proposes candidate case prompts and scoring blueprints from declared construct, role, case grammar, constraints and forbidden exposure patterns.
definitions.scope: Case-bank development, not live scoring or release.
boundaries: A generated prompt is not an approved Case Version.
Novel wording does not establish independent reasoning pattern, solvability or equivalent difficulty.
definitions.intuition: It makes draft questions that experts still have to test and release.

definitions.statement: An Item Bank is a governed inventory of candidate, released, held-out and retired Case Families and Case Versions with identity, exposure, lineage, access and lifecycle records.
definitions.scope: One product and research program version.
boundaries: Bank inclusion does not mean a case is eligible for scored administration.
Restricted cases and answers cannot be treated as public challenge content by default.
definitions.intuition: It tracks which questions exist, how they relate and whether they can still be used.

definitions.statement: A Case Evaluation is a versioned pre-release or monitoring assessment of a Case Version against declared construct coverage, answerability, alternative solutions, difficulty, repetition, exposure, accessibility and timing criteria.
definitions.scope: One case version and intended population or administration context.
boundaries: An automated similarity score is not proof of case equivalence or uniqueness.
Case quality does not establish candidate-score reliability or job prediction.
definitions.intuition: It checks whether a question is usable before and after people see it.

definitions.statement: A Scorer Evaluation is a versioned test of a pinned human or automated scoring procedure against independent anchored ratings, evidence spans, adversarial responses, mode changes and downstream criteria under a declared population and use.
definitions.scope: One scoring version and compatible cases, rubrics and response modes.
boundaries: Agreement with human ratings is not sufficient evidence of construct or predictive validity.
A scorer that matches aggregate distributions may still miss unusual valid answers or create subgroup error.
definitions.intuition: It tests whether the scoring method reads answers correctly and whether its scores mean anything useful.

definitions.statement: A Developer Challenge is the participant-facing, versioned offer of practice, up to three scored case sessions and purpose-limited provisional feedback under one declared administration and data-use protocol.
definitions.scope: One MVP challenge release and eligible audience.
boundaries: The challenge is not a validated hiring selection procedure.
A challenge release does not itself authorize participant data collection.
definitions.intuition: This is the experience offered to developers, with its limits stated before they join.

definitions.statement: An Invitation is a one-use, versioned offer to an eligible person to enter a specified Challenge and Study Protocol, recording source channel and redemption state without assigning a score.
definitions.scope: One recruitment event and participant entry route.
boundaries: An invitation is not research permission.
Redeeming an invitation does not prove eligibility or complete enrollment.
definitions.intuition: It records who was offered which pilot route and whether that route was used.

definitions.statement: A Study Protocol is a versioned prospective plan fixing population, eligibility, purposes, procedures, measures, assignment, exclusions, analysis, stopping rules, custody and decision owners before a pilot or study collects data.
definitions.scope: One formative pilot or named-role validation study.
boundaries: A mixed-developer formative protocol is not role-specific hiring validation.
A draft protocol has no participant-collection authority.
definitions.intuition: It says who joins, what happens, what is measured and how results will be interpreted before answers arrive.

definitions.statement: A Purpose Choice is one attributable participant action about one named processing purpose under an exact notice version, with time, source and later withdrawal or supersession recorded.
definitions.scope: One participant, purpose and notice version.
boundaries: A user-interface choice alone does not determine the lawful basis for processing.
Challenge access does not imply optional research, follow-up, training or employer sharing.
definitions.intuition: The record says what the person chose for one use of their data, under the wording they saw.

definitions.statement: An Assessment Attempt is one participant's version-pinned scored journey under a Study Protocol, containing at most three ordered Session slots and a terminal completion, withdrawal or void state.
definitions.scope: One challenge participation; practice is separate.
boundaries: An attempt is not one Session or one Response.
A retry must preserve its predecessor and reason rather than replace history.
definitions.intuition: It groups the three possible case sessions into one auditable challenge run.

definitions.statement: An Assignment Manifest is a frozen allocation rule and result set binding eligible attempts to case versions, order, arms and response modes with recorded probabilities, strata and randomization provenance.
definitions.scope: One Study Protocol version and its allocations.
boundaries: Allocation cannot be changed after observing an answer without a recorded deviation.
A manifest does not prove case forms are equivalent.
definitions.intuition: It lets researchers reconstruct why each participant saw a particular case and order.

definitions.statement: A Session Assignment is one immutable binding of an Attempt slot to a released Case Version, Rubric, Response Mode and Administration Policy, with any retry linked to its voided predecessor.
definitions.scope: One scored slot and one administration instance.
boundaries: Assignment is not evidence that the participant viewed or answered the case.
A retired case may remain pinned to historical answers but cannot receive new assignments.
definitions.intuition: It freezes the exact task and rules for one slot before the participant starts.

definitions.statement: An Administration Policy is a versioned rule set for case reveal, recorded-time cap, allowed help, pause, retry, device failure and accessible modes applied consistently to a declared population and case set.
definitions.scope: One Challenge and compatible Study Protocol version.
boundaries: A browser timer does not establish compliance with the recorded-time rule.
An accommodation route is not a scoring penalty.
definitions.intuition: It states how the case is delivered and what happens when time or technology fails.

definitions.statement: A Session Event is an append-only, server-timed observation or accepted transition in one Session, with sequence, actor, purpose and causal parent sufficient to replay delivery and failure history.
definitions.scope: One session state or reveal occurrence.
boundaries: An event log is not the answer recording.
Client timestamps are diagnostic and cannot silently override server order.
definitions.intuition: It records when the case was shown, started, revealed, stopped or failed.

definitions.statement: A Media Object is a private, content-digested and duration-verified source recording or chunk set bound to one Session Assignment, capture mode, custody location and retention class.
definitions.scope: One committed source recording version.
boundaries: An upload receipt does not establish the answer's meaning or validity.
Media custody does not grant scorer, research or public access.
definitions.intuition: It identifies the exact recording and where it must be protected or deleted.

definitions.statement: An ASR Run is a version-pinned speech-to-text processing attempt on one Media Object, retaining engine/configuration, status, uncertainty and output Transcript reference or failure.
definitions.scope: One transcription job and source media version.
boundaries: The ASR output is not the source Response.
A successful job does not imply words or reasoning evidence were transcribed correctly.
definitions.intuition: It records how speech became text and whether that conversion failed or lost information.

definitions.statement: A Transcript Correction is an attributable, versioned change proposed or confirmed by a participant or authorized reviewer against one Transcript, preserving the prior text, source alignment and reason.
definitions.scope: One transcript successor version.
boundaries: Correction never rewrites the original Media Object.
Corrected text cannot be treated as an independently recorded spoken answer.
definitions.intuition: It fixes words in the text while preserving what the recording and earlier transcript contained.

definitions.statement: An Answer Evidence Span is a source-linked excerpt or time interval in one Response or Transcript cited for a specific Criterion Rating, with version, location and correction status.
definitions.scope: One rating claim about one answer version.
boundaries: A span is supporting material, not a rating or proof of construct validity.
A text excerpt must remain traceable to the source and its transcription uncertainty.
definitions.intuition: It shows which exact part of an answer led to a rating.

definitions.statement: An Adjudication is a separately attributable resolution of a declared rating disagreement under a pinned rule, preserving all independent ratings, cited evidence and resolution reason.
definitions.scope: One discrepancy within a Scoring Run or calibration exercise.
boundaries: Adjudication does not erase rater disagreement.
A resolved rating is not ground truth about future work performance.
definitions.intuition: It records how a reviewer handled differing judgments without hiding the difference.

definitions.statement: A Research Export is a purpose-filtered, pseudonymized and versioned dataset delivery with exact protocol, eligibility snapshot, field set, source lineage, recipient, expiry and revocation record.
definitions.scope: One approved research extract and delivery.
boundaries: A pseudonym is not proof that reidentification is impossible.
An export receipt does not grant a new purpose or override withdrawal.
definitions.intuition: It says exactly which study data left the application, why, when and for whom.

definitions.statement: A Participant Rights Request is an attributable request for access, correction, research withdrawal or deletion, with verification, affected-record lineage, applicable decision, execution state and response receipt.
definitions.scope: One participant request under the selected privacy protocol.
boundaries: A request is not proof that deletion or correction has completed.
A documented exception must not be hidden as a successful deletion.
definitions.intuition: It tracks what the participant asked for and how the project responded across copies and derivatives.

definitions.statement: A Retention Schedule is an owner-reviewed, versioned mapping from data class and purpose to trigger, expiry, deletion route and documented exception under the selected jurisdiction.
definitions.scope: One Challenge deployment and its data classes.
boundaries: Software defaults cannot select a lawful retention duration.
A schedule is not evidence that deletion ran successfully.
definitions.intuition: It states how long each kind of data is kept and what should happen when that time ends.

definitions.statement: An Access Audit Event is an append-only record of a staff or service action on a protected resource, with actor, purpose, target, time, outcome and causal job reference while excluding answer text and secrets.
definitions.scope: One protected read, write, export or deletion action.
boundaries: An audit event does not itself authorize access.
A log of a requested action is not proof that its downstream work completed.
definitions.intuition: It lets owners see who accessed or changed protected data and for what stated purpose.

definitions.statement: A Challenge Participant is one pseudonymous person identity eligible to enter a declared Challenge, linked to contact and reidentification data only through restricted custody.
definitions.scope: One person within a Challenge deployment.
boundaries: A pseudonym does not make answer data anonymous.
A participant identity does not imply research inclusion or an employment candidate identity.
definitions.intuition: It keeps one developer's challenge records together without putting their contact details in scoring data.

definitions.statement: An Identity Vault is the restricted mapping between a Challenge Participant's pseudonym and contact or reidentification data, with separate access, retention and deletion controls.
definitions.scope: One challenge deployment and its authorized identity operations.
boundaries: A vault is not a research extract or scorer input.
Storing a key separately does not alone prevent reidentification.
definitions.intuition: It holds the information needed to contact a person or answer their data request away from their scored answer.

definitions.statement: A Participant Notice Version is immutable participant-facing wording for one locale and effective period that names processing purposes, controller/contact, recipients, retention references and rights routes by content digest.
definitions.scope: One challenge release and displayed locale.
boundaries: A notice is not proof that it was displayed or understood.
Changing material wording creates a new version and cannot silently revise earlier Purpose Choices.
definitions.intuition: It preserves the exact data-use explanation a developer saw before making a choice.

definitions.statement: An Outbox Job is a durable, idempotent intent to perform one asynchronous operation on pinned records, with status, retries, causal action and completion or failure receipt.
definitions.scope: One media, transcription, export, rights or notification operation.
boundaries: Queued intent is not completed effect.
Retrying must not duplicate a committed export, deletion or notification.
definitions.intuition: It makes background work recoverable without pretending a queued task has already happened.

definitions.statement: A Case Generation Brief is a frozen request for one case-development batch stating session purpose, intended construct, audience, reasoning mechanism target, case grammar, constraints, response modes, language, time budget, forbidden patterns, exposure exclusions and review criteria.
definitions.scope: One case-generation batch for a formative or role-linked study.
boundaries: A brief is not a generated case or a release decision.
A difficulty target is a hypothesis until tested with people.
definitions.intuition: It tells authors and generators what kind of problem is needed and what must be avoided.

definitions.statement: A Case Generation Run is one reproducible execution of a pinned Case Generator against one Generation Brief, retaining model or human author, prompt/configuration, seed where applicable, inputs, all outputs, cost and failure receipts.
definitions.scope: One candidate-producing execution; no live administration.
boundaries: Reproducible inputs do not guarantee identical stochastic output.
A run cannot approve or publish its own candidates.
definitions.intuition: It records exactly how a batch of draft questions was produced, including rejected drafts.

definitions.statement: A Case Candidate is an immutable draft prompt, reveal plan and proposed answer/rubric blueprint from a Generation Run or named human author, linked to its brief, mechanism and development status before release.
definitions.scope: One pre-release draft and revision lineage.
boundaries: A draft is never assignable to a scored participant.
Changing a candidate creates a successor rather than hiding the rejected version.
definitions.intuition: It is a proposed question that still needs screening, testing and independent review.

definitions.statement: A Reasoning Mechanism Fingerprint is a reviewer-visible description of the inference, assumption change, causal model, tradeoff or strategic move needed to solve a Case Candidate, separate from its wording and theme.
definitions.scope: One candidate or family comparison in the Item Bank.
boundaries: A shared topic is not necessarily a shared solution mechanism.
An embedding or model label alone cannot certify distinct reasoning mechanisms.
definitions.intuition: It detects when two different-looking questions rely on the same trick.

definitions.statement: A Case Similarity Assessment is a versioned comparison of a Case Candidate with selected bank and known-public items on surface wording, scenario structure, underlying mechanism, answer leakage and exposure evidence, recording method, thresholds and reviewer resolution.
definitions.scope: One candidate screening pass against a dated comparison corpus.
boundaries: A low similarity score is not proof of novelty or security.
Similarity thresholds and search corpus must be pinned; unseen public items remain possible.
definitions.intuition: It flags both obvious duplicates and rewritten versions of the same puzzle for human review.

definitions.statement: A Case Trial is a consented, non-scored development administration of a Case Candidate under a pinned protocol, capturing time, comprehension, solution paths, accessibility issues and prior exposure for case evaluation.
definitions.scope: One draft and a declared volunteer sample.
boundaries: A trial response does not establish role validity or calibrated difficulty.
Trial exposure changes later reuse and must be tracked.
definitions.intuition: It checks with real people whether a draft question works as intended before release.

definitions.statement: A Case Review is an independent, attributable assessment of a Case Candidate and its Case Evaluation against declared answerability, alternate answers, construct evidence, access, time, cultural/context dependence, similarity and exposure criteria, with unresolved objections preserved.
definitions.scope: One candidate and intended use before release or revision.
boundaries: Reviewer agreement is not proof of predictive validity.
A generator cannot be the sole reviewer of its own output.
definitions.intuition: A qualified person checks the draft and records why it may or may not be used.

definitions.statement: A Case Disposition is an attributable decision under an assigned case-bank role to reject, revise, hold, release or retire an exact case version for a named use, citing reviews, exposure, rubric compatibility and effective time.
definitions.scope: One candidate or released Case Version and use context.
boundaries: A disposition does not admit a definition or authorize participant data collection.
Retirement stops new assignment but does not rewrite historical responses or research evidence.
definitions.intuition: It records who decided whether a question can enter or leave the live bank and why.

definitions.statement: A Question Lifecycle Rule is a versioned, scoped constraint on case development, review, release, assignment or retirement with an identified owner, check, failure handling and affected records.
definitions.scope: One case-bank process and declared version.
boundaries: A documented rule does not execute itself or grant authority.
A research hypothesis about question quality is not an enforced rule until an owner selects a check and response.
definitions.intuition: It says what must hold when a question moves through the bank and what happens when it does not.

definitions.statement: A Question Lifecycle Use Case is an actor's bounded objective in the case bank, identifying trigger, permitted inputs, expected outcome and completion evidence without prescribing every implementation step.
definitions.scope: One actor goal within question development or operation.
boundaries: A use case is not an API operation or authorization.
Completion criteria do not establish that an experiment succeeded.
definitions.intuition: It states what a researcher, reviewer or service needs to accomplish with a question.

definitions.statement: A Question Lifecycle Operation is one idempotent or explicitly non-repeatable action with defined actor, input preconditions, state transition, output records and refusal or retry behavior in the case bank.
definitions.scope: One bounded executable step in the question lifecycle.
boundaries: An operation's success receipt is not scientific validation of the case.
An operation cannot grant owner authority absent an exact prior decision.
definitions.intuition: It is one concrete action, such as screening a draft or releasing an exact case version.

definitions.statement: A Question Lifecycle Workflow is a versioned ordering of case-bank operations, rule checks, review gates and branches from generation brief through draft, release, monitoring and retirement, preserving provenance at every transition.
definitions.scope: One declared question-development route and intended use.
boundaries: A workflow definition is not a run or evidence that all gates passed.
A review checkpoint does not itself authorize a release decision.
definitions.intuition: It is the route a question follows from idea to use and eventual retirement.

definitions.statement: An Application Access Permission is one versioned allow rule for an authenticated principal with an active role assignment to attempt a named action on a resource under exact subject, purpose, state and decision guards, with default denial otherwise.
definitions.scope: One MVP policy version, action and resource class.
boundaries: A permission entry is an application enforcement rule, not a Lab Authority claim or owner decision.
Role membership alone does not satisfy purpose, object or separation-of-duties guards.
definitions.intuition: It states which action the app may allow after checking who, which record, why and under which approved state.

definitions.statement: An Application Access Policy is an immutable versioned set of Access Permissions, default-deny rules, separation-of-duties constraints and evaluation order selected for one deployment and protocol scope.
definitions.scope: One challenge deployment and policy version.
boundaries: A policy file does not activate itself or grant governance authority.
Changing a permission or guard creates a successor version with review and test evidence.
definitions.intuition: It is the complete rulebook the app checks before reading or changing protected data.

definitions.statement: An Access Decision Receipt is an attributable result of evaluating one principal, action, resource, purpose and state against one Access Policy version and active role assignment, recording allow or deny, guard reasons and time without answer content.
definitions.scope: One attempted protected application action.
boundaries: An allow receipt is not scientific evidence or owner authority.
A logged intent or denied attempt is not proof that a downstream operation completed.
definitions.intuition: It records why the app allowed or refused one request under the exact policy in force.

definitions.statement: An Exceptional Access Grant is a short-lived, object- and operation-specific application grant for a documented rights, evidence or incident case, with separate owner approvals, expiry, purpose and use receipts.
definitions.scope: One exceptional access ticket and exact protected objects.
boundaries: It cannot authorize employer sharing, bulk export or a new processing purpose.
An incident label alone does not create this grant or override normal access checks.
definitions.intuition: It allows a narrowly approved staff inspection when ordinary roles lack access, and leaves an audit trail.

definitions.statement: A Session Recovery Rule is a versioned, state-specific prescription for one failure class under an Administration Policy, defining observable detection, what remains valid, timer behavior, same-assignment recovery eligibility, void/replacement criteria, participant message and required audit evidence.
definitions.scope: One failure class, administration-policy version and session state.
boundaries: A rule is not an observed failure or a runtime recovery decision.
A replacement case must be a previously released form selected under the study protocol; a generator cannot authorize an immediate retry.
definitions.intuition: It says exactly what the product should preserve and do when a particular kind of failure occurs.

definitions.statement: A Session Recovery Decision is an append-only evaluation of one affected Session Assignment against a pinned Recovery Rule and observed events, recording the chosen same-assignment resume, wait, technical void, authorized replacement or human review, its reason, evidence, actor and successor link.
definitions.scope: One failure episode affecting one session assignment.
boundaries: A decision receipt does not prove the media is intact or the replacement case is equivalent.
A technical void is not a zero Criterion Rating and does not create a fourth scored slot.
definitions.intuition: It records why the system resumed this answer, waited, or offered a governed replacement.

definitions.statement: A Media Upload Attempt is one resumable transfer of one captured response to a private media object, with server-owned object/upload identity, part receipts, declared and verified checksums, expiry, completion or abort state and causal session assignment.
definitions.scope: One transfer attempt for one response and object key.
boundaries: A part receipt or completed transfer is not a verified Media Object.
A resumed transfer does not restart the session clock or change the assigned Case Version.
definitions.intuition: It tracks which bytes reached storage so a broken connection can resume without recording a new answer.
